residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a bona fide resident of Kansas for at least sixty (60) days immediately preceding the filing of the petition.

waitingPeriod.description: An action for divorce shall not be heard until at least sixty (60) days after the date the petition is filed, unless the judge enters an order declaring the existence of an emergency. K.S.A. §23-2708.

noFault.name: Failure to Perform a Material Marital Duty or Obligation
noFault.description: Failure of a party to perform a material marital duty or obligation

noFault.name: Incompatibility by Reason of Mental Illness or Mental Incapacity
noFault.description: Incompatibility by reason of mental illness or mental incapacity of one or both spouses, requiring confinement for 2 years or adjudication of mental illness, plus a finding by 2 of 3 court-appointed physicians of poor prognosis for recovery

groundsForDissolution.notes: Kansas recognizes three grounds for divorce under K.S.A. §23-2701: incompatibility, failure to perform a material marital duty or obligation, and incompatibility by reason of mental illness or mental incapacity. None are traditional fault-based grounds.

propertyDivision.description: Kansas uses equitable distribution. All property owned by either spouse is subject to division, including property acquired before the marriage. The court divides property in a just and reasonable manner considering the age of the parties, duration of the marriage, property owned, present and future earning capacities, time and manner of acquisition, family ties and obligations, allowance of maintenance, dissipation of assets, and tax consequences.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Kansas does not have a traditional separate property classification. All property of either party is subject to equitable division, though the court considers when and how property was acquired.

legalCitations.description: Grounds for divorce — incompatibility, failure of marital duty
60-day waiting period from filing — action for divorce shall not be heard until 60 days after filing unless emergency declared
Property division — equitable distribution of all property
Child custody — legal custody, residency, parenting time
Kansas Child Support Guidelines — income shares model

filingFees.notes: Kansas statewide base docket fee for divorce is $173 (K.S.A. §60-2001). With surcharges extended by the Kansas Legislature, the total filing fee in most judicial districts is $195 (e.g., Third Judicial District/Shawnee County as of June 2025). Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via a Poverty Affidavit.

basic.name: Domestic Relations Affidavit
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, expenses, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order granting the divorce

service.name: Summons
service.description: Service on respondent via sheriff or process server

service.name: Voluntary Entry of Appearance
service.description: Respondent voluntarily enters an appearance and waives formal service
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Proposed custody, residency, and parenting time arrangement (required per K.S.A. §23-3222)

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Kansas Child Support Guidelines (K.S.A. §23-3001 et seq.)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Kansas Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Respondent must file a response within 21 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Kansas must file a response within 21 days of service (additional time may be granted)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Kansas uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Kansas Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust. Parenting time adjustments may apply.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Kansas allows court-ordered maintenance (not called alimony). The court may award maintenance in an amount the court finds fair, just, and equitable. Maintenance is generally limited to 121 months. Factors include the age and earning capacity of both parties, the duration of the marriage, the property owned, and the ability of the paying spouse to meet both parties' needs.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: The court has discretion but maintenance is not automatic. It is more common in longer marriages with significant income disparity.

court.name: District Court, Division of Domestic Relations
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the District Court, Division of Domestic Relations, in the county where the petitioner or respondent resides.
